topic: A person learns their favorite restaurant is closing
text: I walk into my usual spot, the aromas of garlic and freshly baked bread greeting me like an old friend, but something's off. The familiar hum of the place seems more hushed, the usual warmth of the lighting almost too stark. I take my seat, and as I open the menu, I notice a new, small sign: "Thank you for the memories. Please join us for our last week." My hand pauses mid-air, and the menu feels heavier, the weight of those words sinking in. Each dish, every sip of wine, now carries a bittersweet taste I never expected. I order my favorite, but it's hard to enjoy, knowing each bite is a farewell.
